why: The biggest win comes from pulling business details and inspection findings straight from Pathway and the Eat Safe platform, which needs an Azure integration.
knowledge: Food Standards Code chapter 3 (food safety standards).
Council's approved improvement notice template (Word) and enforcement policy.
Inspection checklist and common non-compliance wording.

steps: Confirm the business owner, scope and success measures, and raise an Azure DevOps card (why and how).
Move the prototype into an Azure DevOps repo and rebuild the front end in Vue and Bootstrap, hosted on Azure App Service with council (Entra ID) sign-in.
Move all AI calls into an Azure Function App, with Claude through Microsoft Foundry or the council's Anthropic agreement. Keys live in Key Vault, never in the page.
Strip or pseudonymise personal information before anything goes to the model.
Load the knowledge into an Azure AI Search index over the legislation, template and policy in Blob Storage, so answers can quote their source.
Pull business and licensee details from Pathway and findings from the Eat Safe inspection platform.
Have Legal Services sign off the notice template and the wording rules.
Save the final notice to the records system against the business.
Build a test plan and an AI evaluation set (real-style questions with expected answers), then run UAT with synthetic or anonymised data.
Security review against the OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps (including prompt injection).
Get ICT-DA, CAB, PGG and Business System Owner approval, with a Go Live plan, service transition document and support playbook.
setup: Dev, Test and Prod resource groups in the council's Azure subscription.
Azure App Service (front end) and Azure Function App (AI and data calls).
Key Vault, Application Insights logging and cost alerts.
Blob Storage and Azure AI Search for the knowledge, or SQL / Cosmos DB for working data.
Model access: a Claude deployment in Microsoft Foundry or an enterprise Anthropic API key (needs an ICT-DA exception as it's outside the listed stack).
Entra ID app registration and a security group for who can use it.
Azure DevOps repo and CI/CD pipelines for Dev, Test and Prod.
Read access to Pathway and the Eat Safe platform (through Boomi or Logic Apps).
Write access to the records system for final notices.

steps: Confirm the business owner, who will use it and what it must never do (it drafts, a person decides).
Set it up as a Claude Project for Environmental Health in the council's enterprise Claude, with the prototype's instructions as the project instructions.
Add the knowledge as project files, or connect the SharePoint library it lives in so it stays current.
Turn the notice drafting into a Claude skill that always uses the approved template.
Have Legal Services sign off the template and wording rules.
Test it with 20 to 30 real-style cases and record how often it gets them right.
Pilot with a small group, give them a 30-minute walkthrough, and collect feedback for two to four weeks.
Get the use case approved (ICT-DA and PGG) and confirm privacy settings before rolling it out wider.
setup: Enterprise Claude seats for everyone who will use it.
A project owner who keeps the instructions and knowledge up to date.
The knowledge in a controlled SharePoint library (approved versions only), plus the Microsoft 365 connector if it's connecting live.
Clear rules on what information can be entered (no unnecessary personal information).
Admin settings checked: data retention, sharing and connector permissions.
Claude seats for Environmental Health officers.
Officers copy findings in by hand, so there's no time saved on data entry.
